newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops said advancing in rebel territory.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops said advancing in rebel territory.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops were reported advancing deeper into northern rebel-held territory on Tuesday after being slowed earlier by counter-attacks by Tamil Tiger guerrillas.

Military officials in the north said the army shelled rebel-held areas northeast of Omanthai on Monday and began moving out of Rambaikulam, which was captured after fierce weekend fighting against the Libertation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
"There was some fighting overnight. They (troops) are advancing," one military official said.
A military spokesman in Colombo declined to confirm the advance, saying he was still waiting for details.
He said troops consolidated their positions in the freshly captured northern areas on Monday, building fortifications and organising supplies.
Troops resumed their drive into the rebel heartland at the weekend after a five-day pause but were slowed by fierce resistance from the rebels. Several soldiers and rebels were killed in the clash.

The Defence Ministry said troops had moved three km (1.8 miles) north of Omanthai to Rambaikulam over the weekend. Security forces last week captured Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of the government-held town of Vavuniya, and Nedunkeni, 40 miles (25 km) northeast of Vavuniya, after a two-pronged thrust into the LTTE's northern Wanni heartland. Vavuniya lies 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
The Defence Ministry said 14 soldiers were killed and 19 wounded in the fighting at Rambaikulam. No casualties were reported on Monday.

Casualty figures released by the Defence Ministry showed 89 soldiers had died in the 14-day old offensive, one of the military's biggest in the 13-year-old ethnic war. About 145 soldiers were wounded.
Hospital sources said about 600 soldiers were wounded.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, but the LTTE say the toll is higher.
Some 20,000 troops launched "Operation Jaya Sikuru" -- "Sure of Victory" -- from Vavuniya on May 13 in a bid to open a supply route to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.
Government forces rely on air and sea links to supply bases and civilians in Jaffna, the LTTE's former would-be homeland brought back under government control last year.

The LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, has accused Colombo of killing Tamil civilians and destroying their property under the pretext of opening a supply route.
Officials in Vavuniya said on Tuesday that the government had agreed to send food into the rebel-held Wanni region, where hundreds of people have been displaced by the latest offensive.

Officials said the government had agreed to send 50 trucks of food and other essential items a day. The military is working out a suitable route for the trucks to be able to move into the Wanni while staying clear of the battle zone.
It was not immediately known when delivery would begin.
Aid workers have said the Wanni's food stocks were strained by additional numbers joining the list and with government supplies to the region grinding to a halt after the latest offensive began.
An overnight statement from the LTTE's international secretariat in London accused the Sri Lankan government of launching a "food-siege" and said the refugee crisis was getting out of control.
